objective: Harden signed AI access sessions so unsafe request resource identifiers are denied before scope authorization and are not echoed in access decisions.

codeReferences.summary: Access decision reason codes now include resource-context-invalid for unsafe request resource identifiers.
Signed-session authorization derives a safeResource before any denial response can include request resource data.
Unsafe signed-session resources are denied before scope checks or admin authorization.
Regression proves path-like signed-session resource ids are denied and not echoed.

redGreenEvidence.command: ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run tests/ai-access-control.test.ts -t "rejects unsafe signed-session resource ids before scope authorization"
redGreenEvidence.observedFailure: The unsafe path-like course resource returned course-scope-denied and was echoed in the access decision.

securityPosture.signedClaims: Previously hardened; unsafe actor and scope ids are rejected as signed-session-invalid.
securityPosture.signedResource: Now denied as resource-context-invalid before scope authorization.
securityPosture.redaction: Unsafe path-like request resource values and signing secret strings are not echoed.
securityPosture.adminBypass: Unsafe resource validation happens before authorizeActorScope, so admin signed sessions cannot authorize path-like request resources.

aggregateEnterpriseGateImpact.summary: This closes another local AI direct-call identity/resource injection edge. The full enterprise gate still requires same-run production env, deployment, storage, ordinary teaching smoke, app-auth, browser-smoke, and live-provider evidence.
